aspects.says: State is replaced by swapping the reference to a new immutable value atomically, so no update is lost and readers see whole snapshots.
A bounded queue blocks producers when full, and offer with a timeout lets a producer give up instead of blocking forever.
A shared map needs ConcurrentHashMap and one atomic call such as putIfAbsent, never a containsKey-then-put.
basis: section:4. Using HashMap in concurrent contexts instead of ConcurrentHashMap

aspects.says: ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent runs its mapping function at most once per key, even under concurrent access.
CopyOnWriteArrayList copies its whole array on every write, so it suits only lists that are written rarely.
basis: section:Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them
aspects.reason: a claim about cost: a test cannot assert allocation or speed; the snapshot behaviour it pays for is practised by 'An event bus that is safe to iterate'

aspects.says: CopyOnWriteArrayList iterates a snapshot, so listeners can change during delivery without ConcurrentModificationException.
A method returning internal state returns a copy, so callers cannot change it outside the lock.
Every class used by several threads should document whether it is thread-safe, for example with @ThreadSafe and @GuardedBy.
aspects.reason: documentation advice with no behaviour a test could check

aspects.says: Shared configuration is safest as an immutable record, validated once and changed only by building a new one.
basis: section:1. Using mutable shared state when immutability would suffice

aspects.says: Expensive work is done outside the lock and only the state change is made under it.
basis: section:3. Holding locks during expensive operations

aspects.says: A BlockingQueue hands work from producers to consumers and does all the synchronization itself.
A ReadWriteLock lets many readers in together and gives a writer exclusive access, which suits read-heavy data.
Prefer no shared mutable state, then shared immutable state, then confinement, then concurrent abstractions, and only then locks.
aspects.reason: the ranking is advice; each strategy on it is practised here in its own right ('Swap an immutable config atomically', 'A service registry without check-then-act', 'Compute outside the lock, store inside it'); thread confinement is practised on 5.1.2 by 'Per-thread request context with ThreadLocal'

aspects.says: Tasks run on executors or structured concurrency are preferred over hand-managed threads.
basis: section:Evolution of Concurrency Best Practices Across Java Versions
aspects.reason: executors and structured concurrency are the subject of the executors and virtual-threads modules (23, 26)

aspects.says: Concurrent code is tested with start gates, bounded awaits and invariant checks, never with sleeps as synchronization.
aspects.reason: the reader does not write tests in these practices; every practice's own grader is written this way

aspects.says: Confining mutable state to one thread, for example with ThreadLocal, removes sharing between threads.
basis: section:The Hierarchy of Safe Concurrency Strategies
aspects.reason: practised on 5.1.2 by 'Per-thread request context with ThreadLocal', where two threads each see only their own request id

aspects.says: A ThreadLocal set on a pooled thread must be removed in a finally block, or the next task on that thread inherits it.
basis: section:2. Forgetting to clean up ThreadLocal in thread pools
aspects.reason: practised on 5.1.2 by 'Per-thread request context with ThreadLocal', which checks that the id is removed when the work ends, also when it throws (on plain threads rather than a pool)

aspects.says: ThreadLocal with millions of short-lived virtual threads costs a copy per thread; ScopedValue or passing context is better.
aspects.reason: a claim about memory cost at scale, which a graded test cannot assert reliably, and ScopedValue is a preview API in Java 21

aspects.says: Collections.unmodifiableList is only a read-only view of a list that can still change; List.copyOf is a real copy.
On Java 21 a synchronized block pins a virtual thread to its carrier during blocking calls, and ReentrantLock does not.
basis: section:5. Using synchronized instead of ReentrantLock with virtual threads

aspects.says: The default non-fair ReentrantReadWriteLock can starve writers under heavy reads; a fair lock serves them in order.
basis: section:3. ReadWriteLock fairness and writer starvation
